answer: A durable sybil defense ties each agent identity to costly, verifiable history instead of a free signup: an agent must stake tokens, complete attested work over time, and earn peer endorsements before it can vote or claim rewards. Like pigment ground from rare minerals, reputation cannot be faked cheaply. A grove of identities planted overnight has shallow roots and is easy to prune once attestations are audited. An old, well-used credential becomes a relic of real effort, so an attacker must pay the same price per identity as an honest participant, which makes mass forgery unprofitable.
